subject: Time For A Fed Rate Hike?

 Good morning! Here's the latest in trending: 

 AI debate:  Meta's ( META ) Zuckerberg and Nvidia's ( NVDA ) Huang push back against AI slowdown.

 No clarity:  Bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) and crypto stocks fall as Clarity Act fails to advance in Senate.

 War fallout: CBO estimates the Iran war cost taxpayers  $38B, while U.S. interceptor supplies  dwindle .
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Top News
 
 
 
 Tough call 
 
 
 
Getty Images
 
 
With the Federal Reserve's policy decision due this afternoon, its chair Kevin Warsh is caught between two opposing forces - markets expecting a rate hike and President ​Trump   pushing for a cut . With  strong jobs data  and inflation still hot , the Federal Open Market Committee is widely expected to raise its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4.00%.

 What to expect:  The odds of a 25-bp rate hike are currently at around 93%, according to the CME FedWatch tool. If the Fed decides to raise rates today, it will be its first hike since mid-2023.  Goldman Sachs believes the FOMC will proceed with the hike primarily to avoid the negative market reaction that would follow if rates were kept on hold. "For the Fed, early September's surging energy prices will probably tip the scale to a hike," said Bill Adams, chief U.S. economist, Fifth Third Commercial Bank. "Consumers may experience higher gas prices viscerally as they drive down the street, but core inflation is more vulnerable to diesel price shocks since businesses mainly use diesel to power their truck fleets." TD Securities expects the Fed to raise rates three times in 2026, starting today. Its previous forecast was that the central bank would hold rates during the year. 

 Cloudy outlook:  Warsh has staunchly defended his view that so-called "forward guidance" — or signaling the likely direction of the FOMC's policy path — isn't useful. So the FOMC's statement will likely only provide commentary on the current decision rather than insight into where rates are heading. As a result, the Summary of Economic Projections, particularly the closely watched "dot plot", will be of significance. But the question remains – can rate hikes bring down inflation? Addison Maier, portfolio manager at Janus Henderson Investors, told S&P Global Market Intelligence that hikes can't impact the price of oil or the outcome of the Iran war, nor change the trajectory of AI spending. However, higher rates could quicken the pace of decline in tariff-driven goods inflation and inflation in the housing sector.

 SA commentary:  "Basically, the Fed must hike, and if it doesn't , it has quite some explaining to do, as a hike is practically fully discounted," ING Economic and Financial Analysis wrote. "One thing market participants will watch is whether the dot plot pencils in more tightening by the end of this year." But SA analyst APAC Research warned that a rate hike could cause stagflation instead of cooling inflation, as higher borrowing costs will strain consumers and businesses without addressing core inflation drivers. SA analyst James Picerno said a pause by the Fed could disappoint the bond market and drive yields sharply higher, while a hike could enrage Trump and possibly imperil the Fed's independence. This leaves the Fed "with an especially difficult choice , a choice that can be summed up as: damned if it does, damned if it doesn't," Picerno said.

NHTSA compels Tesla ( TSLA ) to answer queries about Cybercab .

General Motors ( GM ) CFO expects Q4 to be seasonally weaker .
